clue.text: Soldiers detailed to see the favourite doesn't get nobbled?

definitions.text: Soldiers detailed to see the favourite doesn't get nobbled?

parts.words: Soldiers detailed to see the favourite doesn't get nobbled?
parts.note: read literally, soldiers posted to guard the favourite horse in a race from being drugged; really a British cavalry regiment

explanation.surface: Troops are posted at the racecourse to stop someone doping the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'nobble' a racehorse is to drug or tamper with it so it loses. The regiment's name, read word by word, describes sentries watching a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horse Guards are a household cavalry regiment of the British Army, and so are soldiers.

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian god who notices everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly observant' means watching with a single eye: the chief Norse god gave up one eye in exchange for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-eyed chief god of Norse myth sees with a single eye, and he heads the Norse pantheon.

clue.text: A cleaner type of popular opera

explanation.surface: A question of which musical genre is tidier.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'soap opera' is a long-running TV drama, so the second sense is the popular kind of 'opera'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a washing product, and the name for long-running serial dramas once sponsored by detergent makers.

parts.note: plucky means game, willing and brave

indicators.note: in a down clue, set-up has the word set read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brave arrangement made for fertility cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' works only in a down clue, where reading upwards turns the word over; 'Plucky' is the old sense of game, ready for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproductive cells that fuse at fertilisation; the ova are the female kind.

parts.note: the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, one of Britain's big four lines before nationalisation in 1948

explanation.surface: A famous old railway company ran a charitable fund.
explanation.walkthrough: The London, Midland and Scottish Railway was one of the four big British rail companies before 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or food given to the poor is a form of charitable giving.

indicators.note: an amalgam is a mixture, so the letters of these words are blended together

explanation.surface: A dentist says teeth need a tin filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' means what something is made of: the choppers (teeth) are made up of this tissue. 'Amalgam' doubles as the dental filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are built chiefly of the hard tissue beneath the enamel, so it is what choppers consist of.

parts.note: a game played in chilly weather, such as skiing or skating, rather than an unfriendly one

explanation.definitionFit: Skiing, skating and tobogganing are pastimes of the snowy season, so they are games played in the cold.

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of 28's answer may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, the climber who tackles high rises

explanation.surface: A full list is drawn from another entry, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtained from' links the anagram of 28 across's answer to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A listing of items one by one is a detailed account or count.

parts.note: subscribe in its old sense of writing beneath, and nominal meaning of a name: to write your name below

explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe a document is to write one's name at its foot, which is to put a signature to it.

clue.text: Amsterdam in a complicated plan to bring about world peace

definitions.text: plan to bring about world peace

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Dutch city is involved in an intricate scheme for global harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges the letters of AMSTERDAM with IN; 'a' just links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up weapons on all sides is the policy proposed for ending war.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' is read as the verb meaning to stop a flow, not the adjective meaning loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: To check a flow of blood is to staunch it, and the stalk of a plant or glass holds the top up.

parts.note: a flowering, peppery plant that grows untended among crops; blooming also reads as a mild British oath

explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is a yellow-flowered plant of the cabbage family whose seeds are pungent and which infests arable fields.

clue.text: Spring water that is very refreshing

definitions.text: Spring water that is very refreshing

parts.words: Spring water that is very refreshing
parts.note: not bottled water from a spring but rain falling in springtime, which freshens the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A brief rainfall typical of the fourth month freshens gardens in the spring season.

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of these two words are made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Fees vary for the articles listed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' is the verb, meaning accuses or attributes.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute a fault to someone is to lay it at their door, which is to charge them with it.

clue.text: From which one might take refuge in a street shelter?

definitions.text: From which one might take refuge in a street shelter?

parts.words: From which one might take refuge in a street shelter?
parts.note: the reason for ducking into a bus shelter: wintry weather falling from the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Icy rain mixed with snow is the kind of weather that drives pedestrians under cover.

clue.text: Person who will have to pay protection money

definitions.text: Person who will have to pay protection money

parts.words: Person who will have to pay protection money
parts.note: not a racketeer's victim but the company that pays out on a policy that protects you

explanation.definitionFit: An underwriting company pays out money when the risk it covers occurs, so it provides financial protection.

parts.note: the Roman governor of Britain who crushed a tribal uprising in AD 60 found these people in revolt, not disgusting

explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's tribe in East Anglia rose against Rome and was defeated by the governor Suetonius Paulinus.

clue.text: Kind of golfing shot that could be a piece of cake

explanation.surface: A golf stroke described as easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' wants to mean something easy; here it is literally a portion of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf shot that curves away to the side, and a thin wedge cut from a cake.

parts.note: diet in the sense of a legislative assembly, not food, belonging to Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: The lower house of the Irish parliament is a national assembly, which is one sense of 'diet'.
A particular location, and the verb meaning to catch sight of something.

parts.note: current as a flowing stream of water, not the latest thing: the river that runs through the French capital

explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through the French capital is a body of moving water and a sight for visitors.

clue.text: Wizard place in Spain rebuilt for a Dutch philosopher

indicators.note: in puts the wizard's land inside the reordered country
rebuilt signals that the letters of the country's name are put together in a new order

parts.note: the Wizard of Oz lived in the Land of Oz

explanation.surface: A magical land is reconstructed in Iberia for a thinker from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' reorders the country's letters and 'in' places the wizard's land among them; 'for' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century rationalist thinker born in Amsterdam.

clue.text: Get hold of about a hundred decrepit planes?

indicators.note: about says the jumbled aircraft go around the numeral
decrepit means worn out and falling apart, so the letters of the word are broken up and reordered

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Grab some ageing aircraft, around a hundred of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrepit' rearranges PLANES to ENLASP, and 'about' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something tightly in an embrace is to seize or hold it.

clue.text: News put out but not cleared?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A story is released but not approved for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared' looks like approval for the news; here it means brushed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor that has not been brushed has not had its dirt cleared away.

clue.text: Make a deduction from the shake of a head? Hell, yes!

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
shaking the head is a way of saying no

explanation.surface: Someone works something out from a shaken head and exclaims hell, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hell, yes!' reads as an exclamation; 'Hell' is the definition and 'yes!' an affirming tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's name for the underworld of the damned is a common word for hell.

parts.note: Paris here is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen, not the French capital

explanation.definitionFit: Paris, son of King Priam, came from the ancient city besieged by the Greeks.

parts.note: a wading bird of the shoreline whose name is also a hard lump in timber where the grain runs across

explanation.definitionFit: A wader of mudflats shares its name with a whorl in wood, where the grain crosses.

clue.text: A stake in a giant enterprise

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A share in a huge business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player's opening bet is a stake put into the pot.
It means nothing more than (a mere child), and it is a lake or pond.

clue.text: Venturesome fellow who is skilled at negotiating high rises

definitions.text: Venturesome fellow who is skilled at negotiating high rises

parts.words: Venturesome fellow who is skilled at negotiating high rises
parts.note: high rises reads as tower blocks, and negotiating as bargaining, but it means getting over tall peaks

explanation.definitionFit: A climber of peaks is a daring person who gets over lofty heights.

clue.text: A dance that's a staggering success?

definitions.text: A dance that's a staggering success?

parts.words: A dance that's a staggering success?
parts.note: a Scottish dance whose name is also a verb meaning to stagger, so a success of staggering

explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish dance has the same name as a verb meaning to sway unsteadily.

clue.text: Things said to impress political splinter groups, maybe

explanation.surface: Speeches meant to impress from breakaway factions.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: fragments of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Set routines performed to show off at gatherings, and literally bits of a political faction.
